items.readable_text:
Content:
To multiply a binomial and a trinomial, we take each term of the binomial and multiply it by every term in the trinomial. Then, we simplify by collecting like terms.

Content:
For example, to multiply [MATH: ({\color{blue}{x}} + {\color{red}{3}})] and [MATH: (x^2 + 2x+4),] we multiply [MATH: {\color{blue}{x}}] and [MATH: (x^2 + 2x+4),] and then we add this to the product of [MATH: {\color{red}{3}}] and [MATH: (x^2 + 2x+4).]

Content:
[MATH: (x + 3)(x^{2} + 2x + 4)|=; x(x^{2} + 2x + 4) + 3(x^{2} + 2x + 4)|=; x^{3} + 2x^{2} + 4x + 3x^{2} + 6x + 12]

Content:
Then, we group the like terms and simplify:

Content:
[MATH: x^{3} + 2x^{2} + 4x + 3x^{2} + 6x + 12|=; x^{3} + 2x^{2} + 3x^{2} + 4x + 6x + 12|=; x^{3} + 5x^{2} + 10x + 12]

Example Prompt:
Simplify the product [MATH: (x - 3)(x^2 - 2x + 6).]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
We distribute both terms of the binomial to the trinomial in the second parenthesis. Then, we simplify.
[MATH: \eqalign{
(x - 3)(x^2 - 2x + 6) &= \
x(x^2 - 2x + 6) - 3(x^2 - 2x + 6) &= \
x^3 - 2x^2 + 6x - 3x^2 + 6x - 18 &= \
x^3 - 5x^2 + 12x - 18
}]

items.title: Multiplying Trinomials

sections.normalized_html: Given that [MATH: (3s^2 + 2s - 1)(s^2 + s + 2) = 3s^4 + \bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{a}s^3 + \bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{b}s^2 + \bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{c}s - 2,] calculate [MATH: a+b+c.]

We distribute all three terms of the trinomial in the first set of parentheses to the trinomial in the second set of parentheses. Then, we simplify.

[MATH: (3s^{2} + 2s − 1)(s^{2} + s + 2)|=; 3s^{2}(s^{2} + s + 2) + 2s(s^{2} + s + 2) + (− 1)(s^{2} + s + 2)|=; 3s^{4} + 3s^{3} + 6s^{2} + 2s^{3} + 2s^{2} + 4s − s^{2} − s − 2|=; 3s^{4} + 5s^{3} + 7s^{2} + 3s − 2]

Matching up the coefficients, we find that [MATH: a=5,] [MATH: b=7,] and [MATH: c=3.]

So, we have [MATH: a + b + c = 5 + 7 + 3 = 15.]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
To multiply a binomial and a trinomial, we take each term of the binomial and multiply it by every term in the trinomial. Then, we simplify by collecting like terms.

Content:
For example, to multiply [MATH: ({\color{blue}{x}} + {\color{red}{3}})] and [MATH: (x^2 + 2x+4),] we multiply [MATH: {\color{blue}{x}}] and [MATH: (x^2 + 2x+4),] and then we add this to the product of [MATH: {\color{red}{3}}] and [MATH: (x^2 + 2x+4).]

Content:
[MATH: (x + 3)(x^{2} + 2x + 4)|=; x(x^{2} + 2x + 4) + 3(x^{2} + 2x + 4)|=; x^{3} + 2x^{2} + 4x + 3x^{2} + 6x + 12]

Content:
Then, we group the like terms and simplify:

Content:
[MATH: x^{3} + 2x^{2} + 4x + 3x^{2} + 6x + 12|=; x^{3} + 2x^{2} + 3x^{2} + 4x + 6x + 12|=; x^{3} + 5x^{2} + 10x + 12]

---

Item 2 — Example: Multiplying a Binomial and a Quadratic Trinomial

Example Prompt:
Simplify the product [MATH: (x - 3)(x^2 - 2x + 6).]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
We distribute both terms of the binomial to the trinomial in the second parenthesis. Then, we simplify.
[MATH: \eqalign{
(x - 3)(x^2 - 2x + 6) &= \
x(x^2 - 2x + 6) - 3(x^2 - 2x + 6) &= \
x^3 - 2x^2 + 6x - 3x^2 + 6x - 18 &= \
x^3 - 5x^2 + 12x - 18
}]

---

Item 5 — Example: Multiplying Trinomials

Example Prompt:
Given that [MATH: (3s^2 + 2s - 1)(s^2 + s + 2) = 3s^4 + \bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{a}s^3 + \bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{b}s^2 + \bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{c}s - 2,] calculate [MATH: a+b+c.]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
We distribute all three terms of the trinomial in the first set of parentheses to the trinomial in the second set of parentheses. Then, we simplify.

[MATH: (3s^{2} + 2s − 1)(s^{2} + s + 2)|=; 3s^{2}(s^{2} + s + 2) + 2s(s^{2} + s + 2) + (− 1)(s^{2} + s + 2)|=; 3s^{4} + 3s^{3} + 6s^{2} + 2s^{3} + 2s^{2} + 4s − s^{2} − s − 2|=; 3s^{4} + 5s^{3} + 7s^{2} + 3s − 2]

Matching up the coefficients, we find that [MATH: a=5,] [MATH: b=7,] and [MATH: c=3.]

So, we have
[MATH: a + b + c = 5 + 7 + 3 = 15.]

Item 8 — Example: Multiplying Binomials and Trinomials Containing More Than One Variable

Example Prompt:
What is the coefficient of [MATH: a^2b] in the product [MATH: (a+b)(a^2 + ab + b^2)?]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
We distribute both terms of the binomial in the first set of parentheses to the trinomial in the second set of parentheses. Then, we simplify.

[MATH: (a + b)(a^{2} + ab + b^{2})|=; a(a^{2} + ab + b^{2}) + b(a^{2} + ab + b^{2})|=; a^{3} + a^{2}b + ab^{2} + a^{2}b + ab^{2} + b^{3}|=; a^{3} + 2a^{2}b + 2ab^{2} + b^{3}]

Therefore, the coefficient of [MATH: a^2 b] is [MATH: 2.]
